data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Atalante was a huntress and a nymph, known for her exceptional beauty and strength. She was the daughter of the goddess Aphrodite and the huntsman Schoeneus. Atalante was an unconventional heroine, as she was the only one who could outrun the god Apollo. Her name is derived from the Greek word atalantos, meaning ‘unwavering, unyielding’, which reflected her steadfast determination and courage.
data.etymology: Atalante belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nymph of the hunt.”

She was depicted in ancient art, literature, and sculpture, and her story was retold and adapted in various ways over time. Atalante's story continues to be a source of inspiration for writers, artists, and filmmakers, and her image as a strong and unyielding woman has become an enduring symbol of strength and independence.
data.spiritual_significance: Atalante's story also held spiritual significance for ancient Greeks. As a nymph and the daughter of Aphrodite, she was seen as a divine figure, representing the power of the natural world and the beauty and grace of the goddess of Love. Her unyielding spirit and determination were also seen as noble qualities, and her story was used as a reminder of the importance of perseverance and courage in the face of adversity. For many Greeks, Atalante's story offered a powerful example of the divine harmony between the natural world, the gods, and human beings, and her legacy continues to inspire and challenge us to this day.
